# Locked grid headers keep stale sort arrows and miss header settings

## Context

Found during a manual v13.3 sweep of `examples/grid/issues` on `dev` `af81fc0f86`. Sort by Title, then by State: three headers now show a sort arrow (`#` descending, Title ascending, State ascending), but the Store sorts by State alone. The showcase locks `#` and Title at the start and State at the end, so every sort there leaves stale arrows behind.

## The Problem

`Neo.data.Store#sort` keeps a single sorter (`src/data/Store.mjs:1798`). When a header sorts, `grid.Container#onSortColumn` clears every other header's sort state (`src/grid/Container.mjs:1334`). That clear, `removeSortingCss` (`:1428`), only walks the center `headerToolbar`. Buttons in the locked-start and locked-end toolbars keep their arrow and their `isSorted`.

Three grid-level header configs propagate along the same center-only path. `afterSetShowHeaderFilters`, `afterSetSortable` and `afterSetUseTriStateSorting` (`:588`, `:600`, `:612`) each assign only `this.headerToolbar.<config>`. A locked toolbar takes these configs only when it is cloned from the center one (`#19772`). After a runtime change, its buttons keep the old value: `grid.sortable = false`, for example, leaves the locked headers sortable. A locked toolbar created after the change reverts it too, because `Neo.cloneNeoInstance` starts from the center toolbar's construction configs (`src/Neo.mjs:262`). No shipped example toggles these configs on a grid with locked columns; the unit specs below are the witnesses.

## The Architectural Reality

- `grid.header.Wrapper` owns the locked toolbars `headerStart` and `headerEnd`, created on demand, beside the container's center `headerToolbar`. The left-to-right list of those three is rebuilt inline in three places: `Wrapper#applyColumnButtonOrder` (`Wrapper.mjs:87`), `Wrapper#updateHeaders` (`:224–226`) and `Container#onColumnLockChange` (`Container.mjs:1155`).
- Design authority: the code's own contract. The Store keeps one sorter, and `onSortColumn` clears the sort state of every other header after `store.sort()`. Locked buttons fall outside that walk only because they live in other toolbars.

## The Fix

- `Wrapper#getToolbars()` returns the header toolbars in left-to-right order and skips absent regions. The three inline lists use it.
- `Container#removeSortingCss` and the three `afterSet*` hooks walk `getToolbars()`, so every region gets the same state.
- `Wrapper#updateHeaders` clones a locked toolbar with the center toolbar's current `showHeaderFilters`, `sortable` and `useTriStateSorting`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] In `examples/grid/issues`, after any header sort, exactly one header shows a sort arrow, whichever region holds it.
- [ ] Unit (`test/playwright/unit/grid/LockedColumns.spec.mjs`): sorting a center column clears the `isSorted` of a locked-start and a locked-end button and hides their arrows, and sorting a locked column clears the center's. Red on `dev`.
- [ ] Unit (`test/playwright/unit/grid/LockedSubGridConfigs.spec.mjs`): runtime `sortable`, `useTriStateSorting` and `showHeaderFilters` reach the locked toolbars and buttons, including a locked toolbar created after the change. Red on `dev`.
- [ ] The existing grid unit specs and the grid header e2e specs stay green.

## Out of Scope

- The locked-start body seam in the issues showcase, captured as a separate defect-note.
- #19793's filtered-column header state. It needs the same all-region walk and can reuse `getToolbars()`.
